patch.value: Authorize and execute pm-web reachable-history privacy remediation

Current tracked files have zero detected absolute current-user home paths, private IPv4 literals, private-key headers, or common GitHub, AWS and npm token prefixes, but reachable history contains 137 patch lines with the current-user home path and three distinct non-noreply author email identities across 201 commits. Public history must not be rewritten without explicit coordinated authorization and downstream impact planning.

Inventory every reachable ref and tag; classify absolute paths, identities, secrets, hosted data and personal domains; obtain explicit maintainer authorization before any rewrite; preserve an offline recovery bundle; rewrite atomically across every affected ref when authorized; publish coordinated clone invalidation guidance; rescan current files, package contents and full reachable history to zero approved-scope findings before merge or publication
Current tracked scans, reachable-history patch counts, author-domain counts, GitHub secret-scanning status and repository ref count are recorded without exposing matched private values.
pm-web public Git repository with 316 reachable commits

Scan git log --all --format= --patch for absolute home paths and git log --all --format=%ae for author identities; scan tracked files and reachable history for private IPs, private-key headers, and common token prefixes without printing matches.
The public repository and every published artifact have an explicitly approved privacy boundary with no unreviewed personal or hosted-service data in reachable history.

Current tracked scans are clean for the measured patterns. Reachable history has 137 current-user absolute-home-path patch lines, seven distinct author emails of which three are not GitHub noreply identities, and zero detected private IPv4, private-key-header, or common token-prefix patch lines. GitHub secret scanning reports zero open alerts. No history rewrite is authorized.
Merging or publishing without an approved history boundary can preserve personal host or identity metadata in a public repository and package provenance.
